title: Which of these eight figures can be folded to match?
description: Four patterns of diamond shapes and four figures drawn on squared paper are folded in the mind. The matching fold lines of each figure are found and counted.
teaching_notes: One idea: try the straight folds first, then the corner to corner folds, and count only the folds where the halves cover each other. Watch for students who stop after the first fold they find.

source: Trace each figure and draw the lines of symmetry, if any.
video_script.why: The child tries straight and corner to corner folds in an orderly way on eight figures and counts the matching ones.
video_script.substitution: Trace each figure and imagine folding it straight down, straight across and corner to corner, keeping only the folds where the halves overlap.
video_script.anchor: Eight figures: four patterns of diamond shapes and four figures on squared paper
video_script.payoff_line: Try straight folds first, then corner to corner folds.

final_answer.spoken: one line, two lines, two lines, two lines, four lines, two lines, one line, and four lines

never_show: the full list of counts before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
One diamond above two diamonds that touch: 1 line, the vertical one.
Three diamonds in a row, a large diamond made of four small diamonds, and four overlapping diamonds in two columns: 2 lines each, the vertical and the horizontal.
A square inside a bigger square on the grid, with the inner square divided into four: 4 lines.
The eight sided shape with long vertical sides: 2 lines, vertical and horizontal.
The five sided shape with a flat right side: 1 line, horizontal.
The four pointed star on the grid: 4 lines.
Check: fold along each line found once more.
video_script.design: One idea: an orderly search for matching folds. Assumes the child has found the four folds of a square. The eight figures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The counts follow the worklist; the figures are described in words and could not be seen, so the pairing of each count with its figure is taken from the worklist description order.
